reviews.title: Great fans with great performance.  Bright, vibrant colors.
reviews.comment:
So far, so good.  Colors are great.  They are 140mm so they move the same CFM that my 120mm fans moved at 2000RPM (from the Hyper 212 Evo).  These move 75? CFM at 1500RPM and they are quiet.  Good static pressure considering the CFM and RPM they run at and push air at.
I chose these because I have the Thermalright Aqua Elite 360 V3 for my 5900x and am VERY, VERY pleased with how well it cools my 5900x under high loads.  I was blown away.
So, I went with these Thermalright fans (2x in front of case, 1x in rear) and a Thermalright aRGB hub since my Asus B550-F Gaming Wi-Fi II only has 1x aRGB 5v header (and 2x 12v RGB headers which I don't use and never will).
Worked on the first try.
Hubs don't allow you to control individual fans.  That's the controllers.  Hubs will have all your fans do the same "patterns" at the exact same times, but I didn't mind.  It looks great, works great, fans are great... I love Thermalright.
Not to mention, you can't beat the value for money here.  Zero regrets.  I'd buy them, again.
Well, the ONE negative I noticed was that the fans can not hit pure white.  That requires more expensive fans from what I understand.  "White" has a hint of purple in the color to my eyes.  It's all good, I don't use white, anyways.  It'd be nice to have the option, but oh well, "Starry Night" on Aura Sync is my preferred setting, anyways.
reviews.author: AllThingsTech

reviews.title: Killer Value, Great Performance, Quiet Cooling
reviews.comment:
I got these to replace some Phanteks SK140 fans I bought back in 2020. After 5 years the ones mounted to the top of the case were oscillating and making noise at higher rpms.
I wanted to replace them without breaking the bank and had heard good things about Thermalright. I am so glad I did give these a shot. My motherboard only had one 3 pin ARGB connector so I had to do a bit of rerouting and daisy chaining compared to before, using DRGB connections. Still the end result is quiet fans with good airflow and RGB that may not be as vibrant as the Phanteks fans but it's close enough that I barely notice the difference.
reviews.author: Merticois

reviews.title: Decent quality, phenomenal value
reviews.comment: I have bought three packs a few months apart. Might not be the quietest fans, but when you put enough in your system that you can spin them slowly, they are silent at idle and quiet when my system is under load. I also have a pair in my server to pull air through a restrictive filter and shove it through densely packed drives.
reviews.author: P. Truslow

reviews.title: Best Budget Fans
reviews.comment: Thermalright is my go to brand for great budget fans. All of their fans have been great. They aren't the quietest but they move plenty of air and the price can't be beat.
